policy.hypothesis: For Phenethylamine with AlPhos, bases that are strongest in the same-substrate sources should transfer best; specifically, a BTTP quality anchor at 100 C with moderate-to-long residence time should outperform non-BTTP alternatives, while one BTMG and one DBU high-temperature long-residence probe test whether AlPhos shifts the optimum away from the BTTP-dominated same-substrate pattern.

policy.llm_hypothesis: For Phenethylamine with AlPhos, bases that are strongest in the same-substrate sources should transfer best; specifically, a BTTP quality anchor at 100 C with moderate-to-long residence time should outperform non-BTTP alternatives, while one BTMG and one DBU high-temperature long-residence probe test whether AlPhos shifts the optimum away from the BTTP-dominated same-substrate pattern.
failure_conditions: If AlPhos changes the base preference for Phenethylamine so strongly that BTTP is no longer competitive, the anchor will fail.
If the target optimum lies in short-residence or lower-temperature regions not reflected by the selected long-residence 100 C candidates, this initial design will miss it.
If same-precatalyst transfer is more predictive than same-substrate transfer, DBU/BTMG may outperform BTTP and the stated hypothesis is falsified.
If the hidden best base is MTBD or another unselected family, the chosen set undercovers the relevant categorical space.
